title: arXiv Mathematics daily — Friday, 2026-10-23 batch — 8 notable papers
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart; this is an inferred qualitative ranking of notable recent papers rather than measured popularity. Citation evidence is unavailable and independent attention evidence is sparse for this fresh batch.

sections.title: Lenses make many points: Pure point spectrum disproves Simon's L² conjecture
sections.abstract: For every d≥2 and 0≤σ<1/3, the authors construct with LLM assistance a smooth bounded nonnegative potential, arbitrarily small in a specified supremum-plus-weighted-L² norm, for which −Δ+V has pure point spectrum throughout positive energies, contradicting Simon's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: For each d≥2, 0≤σ<1/3, and δ>0, the authors claim a smooth bounded V≥0 with ‖V‖∞+I_d,0(V)+I_d,σ(V)<δ such that −Δ+V has spectrum [0,∞) and no continuous spectral component; positive spectrum is pure point.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Schrödinger operator on R^d, d≥2; I_d,σ(V)=∫R^d |x|^(1−d+σ)|V(x)|² dx, with 0≤σ<1/3.
sections.unique_caveat: Unrefereed preprint; its delicate multiscale construction has not been independently proof-checked here. The authors disclose extensive LLM assistance and state that they take responsibility for the mathematics.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The claimed counterexample addresses a named spectral conjecture in every dimension d≥2 and is cross-listed in spectral theory and mathematical physics. A math.SP account repeated the announcement, and MathWorld's Simon-conjecture entry cites the 2026 result—early external visibility, not independent validation.

sections.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of 4/3 n
sections.abstract: For a planar thrackle, where each pair of edges meets exactly once, the author proves that a thrackle on n≥4 vertices has at most floor(4(n−1)/3) edges, using a computer-assisted small-case result and a discharging argument.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves m≤floor(4(n−1)/3) for every thrackleable graph on n≥4 vertices.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A thrackle is a plane graph drawing in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a shared endpoint or a proper crossing; finite simple graphs with n≥4.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound improves but does not prove Conway's conjectured m≤n bound. The discharging proof uses computer-assisted verification for graphs with at most twelve vertices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete bound on a long-standing extremal conjecture, cross-listed in combinatorics and two geometry/topology categories. The introduction compares it with the previously cited 18(n−1)/13 bound; the announced 4(n−1)/3 bound is sharper. No independent expert discussion was found in the sources checked.

sections.title: Positive sectional curvature on exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions
sections.abstract: The author constructs exotic spheres admitting strictly positive sectional curvature in every dimension n≡3 mod 4, n≥11, except n≡255 mod 256; finite computations also supply examples in that excluded class below 2^16.
sections.claimed_result: For specified quotients of special S³–S³ bundles, the author computes the Eells–Kuiper invariant and shows it is nonzero for a suitable map in each b≥2 with b≢63 mod 64, yielding exotic positively curved spheres in dimensions 4b+3; additional computations cover some excluded-residue dimensions below 2^16.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Homotopy spheres Σ_{ρ_b,β} of dimension 4b+3, with the stated S³ representation and equivariant map; positivity uses recent metric constructions for this family.
sections.unique_caveat: The general theorem leaves dimensions n≡255 mod 256 outside its proved range; only a finite range of those cases is supplied computationally. The construction depends on prior positive-curvature metric results for the family.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result claims examples in infinitely many dimensions in a setting where the paper says known simply connected examples above dimension 24 were diffeomorphic to compact rank-one symmetric spaces. The paper links archived programs and outputs with a Zenodo DOI.

sections.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
sections.abstract: The authors construct a non-Gaussian, distribution-valued critical two-dimensional KPZ process as a scaling limit of centered log partition functions for critical Gaussian directed polymers and via a renormalized Cole–Hopf transform of the critical stochastic heat flow.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim convergence in law to a nontrivial critical KPZ process, measurable from the critical stochastic heat flow after renormalized Cole–Hopf transformation; they report non-Gaussianity, logarithmic-logarithmic covariance blow-up near the diagonal, and Gaussian fluctuations after averaging on shrinking scales.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional critical KPZ, interpreted through centered log partition functions of Gaussian directed polymers and a mollified stochastic heat flow; the paper's specific renormalization and scaling are essential.
sections.unique_caveat: This 84-page preprint's authors report extensive generative-AI interactions in developing the results; the mathematical claims require specialist scrutiny and are not independently validated here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It connects a singular stochastic PDE to directed polymers and a stochastic heat flow, and is cross-listed in probability and mathematical physics. A public Lean 4 formalization project cites the preprint; that is a checkable follow-on artifact, not verification of the analytic proof.

sections.title: Hydrodynamic and Stochastic Limits of Space-Time Hawkes Processes
sections.abstract: For critical and nearly critical space-time Hawkes processes started from a Poisson field of past events, the authors identify high-density deterministic, threshold stochastic, and sparse locally vanishing limits, with altered fractional-diffusion behavior for heavy-tailed delays.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive deterministic diffusion, measure-valued branching limits, and locally vanishing event measures according to initial Poisson density. Heavy-tailed delays produce fractional diffusion and a superprocess occupation-measure limit with memory terms.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Critical or nearly critical space-time Hawkes processes with a prescribed Poisson past; initial profiles may be bounded with infinite total mass, and the limit depends on reproduction-delay tail and matched observation scales.
sections.unique_caveat: The limit descriptions are tied to these initial conditions and scaling regimes; they do not directly characterize arbitrary Hawkes processes or delay laws.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives a three-regime limit theorem and distinguishes finite-mean from heavy-tailed reproduction delays; a substantial probability result, though with no cross-list or independent attention signal in the sources checked.

sections.title: A semiampleness result for hyperkähler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
sections.abstract: For a smooth hyperkähler fourfold whose Picard group is generated by a nef, nontrivial, non-big line bundle of nonnegative Kodaira dimension, the authors prove that a positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration.
sections.claimed_result: If X is a smooth hyperkähler fourfold, Pic(X)=Z[L], and L is nef, nontrivial, not big, with κ(L)≥0, then some positive multiple of L defines a Lagrangian fibration.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth hyperkähler fourfold; Picard group generated by L; L nef, nontrivial, not big, and of nonnegative Kodaira dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: The Picard-rank-one condition and κ(L)≥0 are hypotheses; the result is not a general semiampleness theorem for higher-dimensional hyperkähler manifolds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A substantive semiampleness/fibration theorem cross-listed in algebraic, complex and differential geometry; the authors also identify unobstructedness and smoothing results as independently useful tools. No independent expert discussion was found in the sources checked.

sections.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
sections.abstract: For full-length Reed–Solomon codes, the author classifies all deep holes at interpolation degrees k+m over every finite field for m=3,4,5,6,7, and proves further uniform bounds and large-field classifications for all m≥3.
sections.claimed_result: For m=3,…,7, no deep holes occur for odd m; for m=4,6, the only exceptions are respectively the Segre sextic and Frobenius-power families, only in dimension two over characteristic-two fields. General m≥3 results impose explicit field-size bounds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Full-length RS_q(k) over F_q, with interpolation degree k+m; unconditional classification is for m=3,…,7, while broader results require stated lower bounds on q.
sections.unique_caveat: The unconditional classification does not cover all m; the uniform large-field hypotheses and remaining finite cases matter, and the author notes independent parallel work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Exact classifications across five excess degrees plus uniform bounds, with cross-listing across information theory, combinatorics and number theory. The author reports finite computations with certificates and deterministic verification programs.

sections.title: Improved Bounds for the Entropic Central Limit Theorem in the Log-Concave Case
sections.abstract: For an isotropic log-concave probability measure μ on R^d, the author proves an entropic central-limit bound of order 1/n whose dimension dependence is the minimum of a polylogarithmic term and d.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves H(μⁿ|γ)≤(C/n) min{1+log(ed)²H(μ|γ), d}, where μⁿ is the law of the normalized sum of n independent samples from μ and γ is the standard Gaussian.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Isotropic log-concave probability measure on R^d; relative entropy to the standard Gaussian for normalized sums of independent identically distributed vectors.
sections.unique_caveat: The result assumes log-concavity and isotropy; the abstract does not claim the same dimension improvement for arbitrary input distributions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The stated bound replaces polynomial dimension dependence in the previous best bound with polylogarithmic dependence in one regime, and bridges probability with information theory. No independent expert discussion was found in the sources checked.
